role_description: Runs AWS Partner Central operations, AWS Marketplace seller activities and partner opportunity tracking. Bengaluru, full-time, 2-5 years.
paper_title: Candidate Screening Form – AWS Partner Operations & Marketplace Specialist
paper_notes: Transcribed verbatim from AWS_Partner_Ops_Marketplace_Candidate_Screening_Form (1).docx. The source document's own numbering skips 8, 9, 13 and 14; the 14 questions it contains are renumbered 1-14 here so they display in a continuous sequence. All questions are free-text. Marks are not used - this is a screening form, reviewed by a human, not a scored test.

questions.question_text: Where are you based these days?
questions.evaluation_criteria: Informational. Note whether the location is compatible with working from the Bengaluru office, and flag any relocation requirement.

questions.question_text: This is a full-time role based in Bengaluru. Are you comfortable with this, and would you be able to work from our Bengaluru office?
questions.evaluation_criteria: Screening gate. Look for an unambiguous yes. Treat a clear no as a knock-out for this role and flag it regardless of the rest of the form.

questions.question_text: How many years of relevant experience do you have, and how much of it has been hands-on with AWS Partner Central and the AWS Management Console?
questions.evaluation_criteria: The role is scoped at 2-5 years. What matters is the split: total experience versus time genuinely hands-on in Partner Central and the AWS console. Check the figure is consistent with the task-level answers in questions 5, 6 and 7. Treat 'worked alongside the AWS team' without personal hands-on time as a weaker answer.

questions.question_text: How would you define your current role, and how do you see yourself fitting into this AWS Partner Operations & Marketplace Specialist position at Valamm.AI?
questions.evaluation_criteria: Two parts, both needed: an accurate description of what they do today, and a considered link to this role showing they understand it is an operations and marketplace role rather than a sales or engineering one. Credit realistic self-assessment including gaps.

questions.question_text: What have you personally done inside AWS Partner Central? Please describe the tasks you owned.
questions.instructions: For example: maintaining partner / organization details, APN program requirements and validations, tracking opportunities or referrals, working with AWS partner teams.
questions.evaluation_criteria: Core competency question. Look for named, owned tasks: partner profile and organisation maintenance, APN programme requirements and validations, tier or competency work, ACE opportunity submission and referral tracking, funding or MDF requests, and working with a Partner Development Manager or Rep. The distinction between what they did themselves and what they observed is the signal. Deduct for a description of Partner Central as a concept with no personal tasks.

questions.question_text: Have you worked on AWS Marketplace seller activities? Describe any listing you created, updated or published, and what your role was.
questions.instructions: For example: SaaS listing, product updates, pricing / private offers, publishing and approval workflow.
questions.evaluation_criteria: The other core competency. Look for real listing work: seller registration, listing creation or updates, pricing model chosen (contract, subscription, metered), private offers issued, the publishing and AWS review workflow, and how rejections or revisions were handled. Credit anyone who has taken a listing through to transacting. Deduct for generic Marketplace knowledge with no listing they can point to.

questions.question_text: Which tasks have you done yourself in the AWS Management Console?
questions.instructions: For example: creating IAM users, roles and policies; launching or managing EC2 instances; managing accounts and regions; permissions and access requests.
questions.evaluation_criteria: Tests practical console competence, not architecture skill. Look for specific tasks actually performed - IAM users, roles and policies, EC2, account and region management, handling access requests. Credit an understanding of least privilege. An honest short list of things genuinely done beats a long list that reads like the console navigation menu.

questions.question_text: Have you worked on connecting AWS Partner Central or AWS Marketplace with a CRM? Please describe briefly.
questions.instructions: For example: Salesforce, HubSpot, AWS Partner CRM Connector, opportunity sync.
questions.evaluation_criteria: Differentiator rather than a requirement. Credit real integration work: the AWS Partner CRM Connector, opportunity or referral sync, field mapping, and how sync failures or duplicates were handled. An honest 'no, but I maintained the data manually and here is how' is worth partial credit.

questions.question_text: Do you hold any AWS certifications? Have you used the AWS CLI or AWS APIs?
questions.instructions: For example: Cloud Practitioner, Solutions Architect – Associate, SysOps Administrator.
questions.evaluation_criteria: Informational with upside. Note named certifications and whether they are current or lapsed. CLI or API use signals a candidate who can automate rather than only click through the console - a clear plus for an operations role. Absence is not disqualifying at this level.

questions.question_text: Have you worked at a SaaS company, a technology partner organization, or within the AWS ecosystem before? Please describe briefly.
questions.evaluation_criteria: Look for relevant environment experience: an ISV or SaaS vendor, a consulting or technology partner, or a role inside the AWS ecosystem. Credit understanding of how partner and vendor organisations actually operate. Name the companies where possible so the claim is checkable.

questions.question_text: Tell me about a recent success in your current role.
questions.instructions: Please use a real example and include the outcome.
questions.evaluation_criteria: Look for a recent, specific achievement with a measurable outcome and a clear account of the candidate's own contribution as distinct from the team's. Credit an explanation of why it worked and what was repeatable. Deduct for stale or vague examples.

questions.question_text: Tell me about a recent failure or mistake you've had, and why.
questions.instructions: For example: a listing rejected, wrong permission given, missed deadline, or something else.
questions.evaluation_criteria: Tests self-awareness, and in an operations role the nature of the mistake matters. Look for a real error owned without deflection, an honest root cause, and a specific control or habit adopted afterwards. A permissions or access mistake handled well is a strong answer. Deduct for a humblebrag, a trivial example, or a claim of no mistakes.

questions.question_text: What is your current notice period, and how soon could you join if selected?
questions.evaluation_criteria: Informational, for offer planning. Look for a clear notice period and a realistic earliest start date. Note any buyout requirement; do not penalise a long notice period on merit.

questions.question_text: What is your current CTC, and what is your expected CTC (fixed + variable, if applicable)?
questions.evaluation_criteria: Informational, for compensation alignment only. Look for both figures with a fixed/variable split. Do not judge the candidate on the amounts; note only whether the expectation sits inside the approved band for this role.

questions.question_text: Please share your convenient days and preferred time slots so that we will try to schedule the calls accordingly.
questions.instructions: For example: Tuesday to Thursday, 10:00 AM - 1:00 PM IST. More than one option helps us find a time that works for everyone.
questions.evaluation_criteria: Scheduling information. Look for at least one day with a time slot; several options make the panel easier to arrange. Note any constraint the candidate mentions (notice period, current-employer hours, time zone) and pass it to whoever books the calls.
